entry.hypotheses_domain: Any set of distinct points in real Euclidean plane with at most two positive distances between different points; empty, singleton and infinite sets included. The attaining example is a regular pentagon.

entry.reconstruction_A: Assume six points. In any two-coloring of K6, a vertex has three same-color neighbors. An edge of that color among them closes a triangle with the vertex; otherwise their three edges make the other-color triangle. Thus six two-distance points contain an equilateral triangle. Scale its side to1 and choose A=(-1/2,0),B=(1/2,0),C=(0,h),h=sqrt3/2. Use an additional allowed positive r!=1, choosing any unused value if necessary. Every external P has at least two equal distances to these vertices. If all three equal, subtract squared equations to force P=O=(0,h/3), common square1/3; all1 impossible. If PA=PB=1, x0,y=+-h, and +h is already C, leaving (0,-h), r²3. Rotating vertex roles yields exactly(0,-h),(1,h),(-1,h), all mutual squared distances4, so at most one. If PA=PB=r,PC1, then x0,y=h+-1 and r²=2+-sqrt3. Fixed r fixes its sign and leaves three candidate points at120-degree rotations about O. Their mutual square is3(2h/3+-1)²=2r², neither r²>0 nor1; the latter equality would force3=9/4. The four possible r² values are distinct, so no fixed r mixes cases. At most one external point joins the triangle, hence at most4, contradicting six. Any larger/infinite set has six distinct points. Regular pentagon has its two chord-length types and5 points, proving sharpness.

entry.boundary_probes: At most two includes zero/one distance and0/1/2 points. Choosing an unused r only enlarges the allowed family, and every original pair still lies in it. Equilateral side>0 because vertices are distinct, so scaling divides by a nonzero length. h>0; denominator2/3 nonzero in R. P=C excluded explicitly. Both values2+-sqrt3 are positive but cannot mix for a fixed r; candidates at120degrees are exactly the three singular-vertex choices, not six extra points. Infinite sets reduced to six finite points.
